scope: Empirical and theoretical organizational behavior research across individual, team and organizational levels.

issue.label: Human–AI teamwork
issue.status: Published issue, not an open call

calls.label: Rethinking organizational change
calls.summary: Study how change actually unfolds and is experienced. The call challenges substituting readiness or attitudes for the change process itself.
calls.question: When do employees’ perceptions of change diverge from observable changes in work routines?
calls.design: Proposed design: repeated observations of routines alongside employee accounts; justify temporal spacing and levels of analysis.
calls.risk: A standard attitudes survey may not address the call’s conceptual challenge. A new longitudinal project may not be ready by February.

calls.label: Chronic illness in working life
calls.summary: Investigate ongoing physical illness as an organizational phenomenon, including disclosure, fluctuating symptoms, accommodations and employment relationships.
calls.question: How does day-to-day variation in symptoms change disclosure and accommodation negotiations at work?
calls.design: Proposed design: participant-sensitive diary research with interviews; establish access, consent, privacy and a defensible sampling plan first.
calls.risk: Generic stress or burnout without an underlying chronic condition is outside this call. The PDF also mentions July 1 in prose; its date table and publisher listing end June 30. Confirm with editors; plan for June 30.

calls.label: Review / conceptual idea pitch
calls.summary: An eight-page body-text proposal for research not yet begun. Full review or conceptual papers have a separate, year-round route.
calls.question: Which apparently competing explanations can be reconciled into a useful account of an organizational phenomenon?
calls.design: Proposed approach: preliminary literature scoping, a clear theoretical tension and a development plan. Do not complete the proposed research before using this pitch route.
calls.risk: An invitation following proposal review does not guarantee acceptance of the eventual manuscript. The newer call specifies eight pages; the general author page still describes ten.

calls.label: Propose a special issue
calls.summary: A proposal to organize and edit a special issue. This is a different task from submitting your own research paper.

checks: Make the main manuscript anonymous and prepare author details separately.
Use an unstructured abstract of at most 200 words and no more than five keywords.
Prepare a data availability statement; explain reuse of a dataset in a transparency table where applicable.
Disclose substantive AI assistance as required by the journal; authors remain responsible for accuracy.

Check preprint permission with the editorial office: the current author page asks that manuscripts not be publicly available online. Do not assume a general publisher policy overrides this instruction.
Read the specific call for its article type, length and deadline; specific newer instructions can differ from the general page.
